A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CADmium work. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, experiments, equations, figures and all appendices despite repagination and some layout defects.

before.justification: v1 reports original CAD-generation experiments, model-size and annotation-quality ablations, annotation statistics, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports revised statistical tables and additional qualitative reconstruction comparisons.

M1.justification: The GPT-4.1 annotation pipeline, Qwen2.5-Coder models, LoRA fine-tuning, JSON representation, training objective and greedy decoding remain unchanged in Section 3 and Figure 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepCAD with CADmium and Text2CAD annotations, Fusion360 Reconstruction, and human-annotated CADPrompt. Figure 3's additional examples come from the existing CADmium test set.

E2.justification: New Figure 3 directly compares Qwen's reconstructions with CADmium-trained Text2CAD. v1 evaluated this Text2CAD variant in its separate annotation-quality ablation, while its direct CADPrompt baseline used Text2CAD trained on Text2CAD annotations. Comparator membership in the retained quantitative tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds mean Chamfer Distance reporting and revises reported watertight sample counts in Appendix B. Table 6 changes from 5,433 for every model to 6,205/6,408/6,575/6,779. These unequal counts conflict with the retained common-subset description, leaving the actual evaluation cohorts unclear. Training budgets, benchmark splits and decoding remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds six comparative reconstruction cases, showing Qwen successes, failures and differences from Text2CAD. The model-size and annotation-quality ablations, annotation examples, and Appendix D's metric-specific failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 replaces across-sample standard deviations with 95% confidence intervals and extends interval reporting to medians and binary metrics. Section 4 introduces paired and unpaired hypothesis tests, adjacent-size comparisons, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Both versions still describe a single model run; additional training runs are not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds mean Chamfer distances throughout Tables 1-8 and qualitative outcomes in Figure 3. Tables 6-7 revise topology scores; for example, Table 6's 14B DMCD (x10^3) changes from 1.55 to 1.95 alongside changed sample counts, preventing a same-setting performance interpretation. Tables 4 and 8 swap training/evaluation header roles, reassigning off-diagonal results. Table 5 omits Qwen's previously reported 0.67 EECM point estimate.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for sphericity, SD, DMCD and EECM remain equivalent. No substantive assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: improved annotations, text-to-text CAD generation through code-LLM fine-tuning, structural evaluation metrics and competitive generation performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of annotation conciseness versus completeness, architectural validity, model scaling and annotation-distribution mismatch remain unchanged. Limitations concerning diverse human prompts and high-Chamfer outliers, plus future multimodal editing, are retained.

D1.justification: Optimizer and LoRA settings, hardware, training duration, data filtering and Appendix C's prompts are retained. Code, dataset and model access information and licenses remain equivalent; the links and license sections are relocated.

R1.justification: The same 31 cited works and substantive positioning relative to Text2CAD, CAD-MLLM, FlexCAD and other prior research remain. References are reordered and converted to author-year citations.

P1.justification: Changes include the statistical-testing paragraph, expanded captions, author information, small terminology corrections and an empty comparative-analysis Appendix E heading. The existing narrative and section organization otherwise remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the document template, headings, headers and table formatting, adds Figure 3, and enlarges and redistributes appendix figures. Tables adopt interval brackets and significance-based boldface. The enlargement also places Figure 10's caption below the visible boundary of page 25.

improvement.justification: Confidence intervals, explicit significance tests and comparative success/failure examples improve transparency. However, v2 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies: Tables 6-7 give unequal watertight counts despite claiming common subsets, and Table 8 reports EECM 0.77 with an unexplained interval of [0.78,0.80]. Revised topology scores lack a clear cohort explanation. These issues affect the reliability of the new statistical reporting, so the PDFs do not establish whether the benefits outweigh the added ambiguity.
